author: Pelican State News
title: John Brady to be inducted into Louisiana Sports Hall of Fame in Natchitoches
text:
John Brady to be inducted into Louisiana Sports Hall of Fame in Natchitoches
Former LSU men’s basketball coach John Brady will be inducted into the Louisiana Sports Hall of Fame during a ceremony in Natchitoches, according to a June 24 announcement. The event, part of three days of festivities from June 25-27, will also honor three other LSU athletes and coaches. The induction follows Brady's recent recognitions by the LSU Athletics Hall of Fame last fall and the Louisiana Association of Basketball Coaches Hall of Fame in May.
Brady’s coaching journey began after his graduation from Belhaven College in 1976 when he pursued a master’s degree at Mississippi State and started making connections that would shape his career. "I’m telling you, the dominoes were falling, and I didn’t even know what was going on," Brady said. His mentors included high school coach Bobby Nelson and college coach Charlie Rugg, as well as college head coaches Kermit Davis Sr., Bob Boyd, Richard Williams, and Tim Floyd.
Brady’s early career saw him lead Crowley High School to success before moving through assistant coaching roles at Mississippi State and UNO. He became head coach at Samford University in Alabama, turning around a struggling program before returning to LSU as head coach following Dale Brown's retirement. Despite NCAA sanctions affecting scholarships early in his tenure at LSU, Brady led the Tigers to an SEC title and Sweet 16 appearance in 2000.
His most notable achievement came during the 2005-06 season when he guided LSU to another SEC title and its first Final Four since 1986. Former player Stromile Swift said at a reunion event, "I appreciate you coach... I needed a coach like you. He was a tough coach, and he made us better." Dale Brown also reflected on their relationship, "I didn’t like John Brady at first... But I grew to admire and respect him as a coach and a man. He did a wonderful job with his Final Four team." Tim Floyd added, "He didn’t take any shortcuts... His greatest strength was holding great players to a standard and making them accountable."
After leaving LSU midway through the 2007-08 season amid injuries on his roster, Brady coached Arkansas State until retiring in 2016. He later received additional recognition for contributing talent that helped subsequent coaches win championships at LSU.
Reflecting on his career path leading up to multiple hall of fame inductions, Brady said, "I didn’t leave LSU all mad... And coming back to do radio helped my legacy by people seeing me in a different light... I’m just so humbled by it and these Halls of Fame. I’m a lucky guy."
